title: Cap. VIII: Feeble collection — nothing beyond prior refutations
pass_a_gloss: Placeus answers that this argument has no muscle that was not already in the earlier opposition-arguments, and those have been refuted at length. He asks how thin the collection is: because κρίμα (judgment / guilt from Adam) is set opposite Christ's δώρημα, does it follow that, since the gift does not mean an inhering quality, the κρίμα also cannot mean one?
pass_b_english: I see no strength in this argument that is not already present in the earlier ones, now amply refuted. For how weak this collection is: Here κρίμα, judgment or guilt from Adam, is set opposite Christ's δώρημα. Therefore, as the one does not signify a quality inhering in us, neither does the other?
source_text: Nihil roboris in hoc argumento video, quod non extet in superioribus jam abundè refutatis. Quae enim & quam imbecilla est haec collectio; Hic κρίμα judicium sive reatus ex Adamo, opponitur δώρημα Christi. Ergo ut hoc non significat qualitatem nobis inhaerentem, sic nec illud?

choices.decision: Feeble collection — keep rhetorical question force
δώρημα ... κρίμα pair in the Ergo clause
